Stops 6-9 omit 'lines' because trunk adds a line to sorted_array_proofs.ml and a warning to the expect output of talk_midpoint_overflow.ml.
title: Binary search and sorted updates
summary: `Sorted_array` is a persistent sorted array of `int`s with searches, insertion and removal proved against its elements. The search is written once, over any predicate on indices, and computes its midpoint as `left + (right - left) / 2`. Vox's logic treats `int` as 63-bit wrapping arithmetic, so the textbook `(left + right) / 2` is rejected with a counterexample.

The tour reads the interface, a client and a rejected client, the abstract type and its invariant, the search and the overflowing variant, how the search is used on arrays, and what insertion trusts. The [catalogue page](demo:binary-search) states the claim, the trusted base and the scope.

stops.title: The pure sequence edit model
stops.text: Insertion is `take position source` followed by the value and `drop position source`. Removal joins the prefix with the suffix after the removed position. These are pure functions over sequences; the public edit predicates require exact equality of `contents` with these outputs. Position bounds and sortedness constrain the permitted choices.

stops.title: The model and the search contracts
stops.text: `contents` is the full immutable sequence observation; `contents_length` and `contents_at` tie it to run-time length and indexing. Sortedness is given by `ordered`. The equations for `occurs_between` and `range_spec` give the search meaning: membership, unique equal-value boundaries and first/last matching indices. Insertion and removal are exact sequence equalities to the pure model, with valid positions and length changes.

stops.title: Insertion and removal preserve every other element
stops.text: `insert` returns a valid position and an array whose `contents` equals the model insertion; it may choose any position compatible with sortedness. `remove_at` requires a valid position and returns the model removal. `remove_one` removes the first matching position or returns `None` exactly for absence. `inserted_at` and `removed_at` are derived pointwise consequences; the Boolean element traversal is private proof machinery.

stops.title: A client proof
stops.text: `round_trip` inserts a value and removes the returned position. It proves equality of the entire observed sequence with the source by unfolding the model and using the checked sequence laws for splitting append and composing drops. The derived pointwise lemmas retain its indexed observation guarantee. The client also checks every operation against lists on 121 sequences, including duplicates.

stops.title: A rejected client: a failed search is not membership
stops.text: `(() : {u : unit | p})` asks the checker to prove `p` at that point. When `find_first` returns `None` its contract gives `not (occurs source value)`, so the claim that the value occurs is rejected. This expect test compiles `sorted_array.mli` with `-principal` and checks four rejections: this one, removing index 0 from `empty` (the error points at `remove_at`'s ghost bounds argument), using an `int iarray` as a `Sorted_array.t`, and claiming that `insert` puts the new element at position 0.

stops.title: The abstraction: a refined iarray
stops.text: The representation is a refined integer array: sorted and with length-plus-one not wrapping. `contents` is the immutable sequence observation. The edit predicates use the pure sequence model; `edited` is a private element traversal used only by `edited_contents` to bridge the existing array-copy proof to exact sequence equality. No client needs its Boolean insertion/deletion flag or recursive suffix invariant.

stops.title: The search, over any predicate
stops.text: `Binary.search_midpoint p lower upper` finds adjacent `left` and `right` with `not (p left)` and `p right`, given that `p` is false at `lower` and true at `upper`; it does not need `p` to be monotone. The invariant of `loop` states both `left < right` and `0 < right - left`: with wrapping arithmetic the first does not imply the second. `evaluate` calls `p` only strictly between `lower` and `upper`, so the two ends can be sentinels outside the array. The midpoint is `left + half` with `half = (right - left) / 2`, and the refinement on `index` checks that it lies strictly inside. `divide` is `%divint` declared with a nonzero-divisor refinement, which is assumed, and the loop terminates by `[@@decreases right - left]`.

stops.title: Rejected: the overflowing midpoint
stops.text: This test, written for the talk, copies `Binary` twice and changes one line. Here the midpoint is `divide (left + right) two`. In Vox's logic `int` is 63-bit two's-complement arithmetic that wraps, as the machine does, so the refinement `lower < i && i < upper` on `middle` fails, and the checker's counterexample has `upper = max_int` and a `left + right` that wraps to a negative number. The expected output counts lines from the start of the phrase. The `Safe` module below, with `left + half`, is accepted with the same contract.

stops.title: From a predicate to an array: sentinels at -1 and length
stops.to: let result = Binary.search_midpoint p lower upper premise in
stops.text: `bounds` instantiates the search at `lower = -1`, `upper = Iarray.length array` and `p = above array target strict`, which is false at negative indices, true at and after the length, and in between compares the element with `target`. The premise `0 < Iarray.length array + 1` is the invariant of `Sorted_array.t`; it is what makes `upper - lower` positive. `equal_range` calls `bounds` twice, with `strict` false and true, to get the first index whose element is at least the target and the first whose element is greater. The ghost block builds the search's premise by unfolding `p` and `above`. Sortedness enters later, in `partition`, which proves that everything before the boundary is on one side.

stops.title: Insertion, and what it trusts
stops.to: let result = Iarray.append (Iarray.append prefix [: value :]) suffix in
stops.text: `insert` finds the position with `equal_range` and builds the result from `Iarray.sub` and `Iarray.append`; the ghost block that follows proves `edited` with the local recursion `certify` and sortedness with `Vox_iarray.Int.sorted_intro`. The checker has built-in models of `Iarray.sub` and `Iarray.append` (`normal_iarray_copy` in [`vox_vc.ml`](src:verification/vox_vc.ml)): on normal return it assumes that the bounds of `sub` were valid and that the length of `append` did not overflow. Because it does not know the runtime's size limit, the public `insert` in [`sorted_array.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/sorted_array.ml) checks at run time that `length + 2` does not wrap. [`collections_boundary_check.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/collections_boundary_check.ml) checks, textually, in the Lambda dumps that the run-time operations call no `_def` lemma or proof function.
